  \caption{The retrieval ladder over the 81 GPBam cases: what each pipeline finds, and what that buys the essay. \emph{RRF} rank-fuses a dense and a full-text search; \emph{re-rank} reorders that pool with Qwen3-Reranker-4B; \emph{cite-only} resolves by exact key the norms a second rewriter pass names as applicable, without searching; \emph{cite+RRF} fills the remaining budget behind them; \emph{cite+LS+RRF} also resolves the Normenketten of the retrieved Leitsaetze; \emph{oracle} supplies the statutes the reference solution cites, a bound rather than a system. The last block is the mechanism behind the second: the share of the solution's cited norms that the essay cites too. Columns are ten passages unless marked $k{=}50$, which is also each recall row's budget; blank cells are arms not yet run, and the omitted legs -- dense alone, full-text alone, and hybrid under a round-robin sub-query merge -- are within noise of RRF. Shading is the difference from the block's own baseline (RRF above, no RAG below), blue better, so it reads down a block and not across; bold is a paired difference beyond twice its standard error, which is what separates two cells the judge grid prints as equal. Scores are per-case medians over three free judge seats (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, gpt-oss-120B); the no-RAG column was judged in a separate invocation and the seats are sampled, so a level offset of up to $1.9$ points sits under every difference taken against it, which the printed standard errors do not carry.}
  \label{tab:ladder}
\end{table}

  \caption{What the Bavarian half of the corpus is worth, over the five generators that ran both. The federal corpus contains no state law, so its state-law recall is zero by construction while its overall recall is barely distinguishable -- overall recall is the wrong number to report here. Adding the Bavarian half recovers that recall without converting it: no generator moves by twice the standard error of the paired difference. The retrieval rows hold the pipeline at RRF, so they read at the same setting as Table~\ref{tab:ladder}; the essay rows are the round-robin arms on both sides, the only fusion generated over both corpora. Rows and shading follow Table~\ref{tab:ladder}; the baseline column is the federal corpus.}
